look_here_first: Look for a many-branched, persistent-leaved (evergreen) woody shrub with opposite, serrate, typically 3–5 cm leaves on short 3–10 mm petioles and white to faintly pinkish rayless heads. A. altissima has herbaceous stems and smoother/glabrous cypselae. Mature A. havanensis cypselae are HISPID (hairy).

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Rounded shrubby plant, often woody at the base.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Opposite, ovate to triangular-ovate, serrate, often aromatic when crushed.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Small white discoid heads in terminal corymbs or panicles.

key_traits.label: Fna confirmation
key_traits.text: FNA: shrub 69–150 cm (rarely 30–200 cm), petioles 3–10(–15) mm, deltate to broadly ovate (sometimes hastate) leaves generally 3–5 × 2–5 cm; leaves essentially gland-free; involucres 4–6 mm; foliage persistent in the US flora.

key_traits.label: Mature cypsela
key_traits.text: Hispid (hairy), contrasted with glabrous A. altissima (FNA).

key_traits.label: Leaf persistence
key_traits.text: Persistently leaved / evergreen shrub, rare within Flora of North America Ageratina.
